title: U.S. House · Colorado's 3rd District
area: Western Slope and southern Colorado, including Grand Junction, Durango and Pueblo.

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Hurd defeated Ron Hanks in the Republican primary. Dwayne Romero defeated Alex Kelloff 54.8%-45.2% in the Democratic primary. This district was a closely watched swing seat in the 2024 election.

candidates.name: Jeff Hurd

priorities.text: Lowering household energy costs, opposing state and federal regulations he says push families toward more expensive heating and electricity options.
Co-led a bipartisan framework (the HOPE Act / "CommonGround 2025") to temporarily extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits with new income caps and anti-fraud safeguards.

positions.summary: Criticized state and federal climate-driven regulations that push households and utilities away from natural gas toward electric heat pumps and other mandates, calling the added costs a "hidden tax" on families.
positions.quote: I’m fighting those in Congress for the same reason I’m fighting this one: working families should not have to bankroll regulatory experiments. Energy policy should start with common sense, not mandates.

positions.summary: Co-led the bipartisan HOPE Act to extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits for two years, with new income caps and anti-fraud provisions, to prevent a spike in health-insurance premiums.
positions.quote: The HOPE Act is a practical, bipartisan solution that maintains affordability, enhances transparency, and improves accountability while Congress works toward long-term reforms that will make our health-care system more stable and more affordable.

positions.summary: Told CPR News he is concerned that broad tariffs increase costs for consumers and that tariffs should be used with caution; the report notes he voted against President Trump's tariffs.
positions.quote: because those costs can get passed directly to Colorado consumers, to farmers and to businesses

record.text: Chairs the House Natural Resources Committee's Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee and serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: As a sitting member of Congress, detailed floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. Issue positions above are drawn from his official House website's Issues and Media sections.

priorities.text: Lowering cost of living: proposes repealing tariffs he says are raising fuel and grocery prices, and expanding the Family Tax Credit.
Protecting Colorado's water resources amid Colorado River Compact challenges and drought.
Supporting family farms and ranches with a robust Farm Bill and restrictions on foreign ownership of Colorado water and farmland.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to repeal what he calls 'disastrous tariffs' that are raising the cost of living for the district.
Describes an 'all-of-the-above' energy approach that uses the district's existing energy resources while also advancing alternative energy deployment.
Calls for building more housing, repealing what he describes as outdated construction red tape, and stopping large investors from buying up homes to drive up rents.
Told CPR News he would work to repeal parts of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, including its cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.

candidates.name: Clifton Brown

priorities.text: Pledges not to take money from any corporation or PAC and not to earn more than the government salary.
Says gerrymandering should stop and calls for ending congressional districts.
Calls for a "citizen protection act" limiting voting, campaign contributions and real estate ownership to citizens.

candidates.researchNotes: Unaffiliated. Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (2026); his survey mentions the site ruhero.com, which was not fetched. His answers do not directly take a side on most listed issues.

statements.quote: I believe that saving the planet is our biggest responsibility as Americans.
